how.title: Google Ads in plain English
how.text: You choose the searches you want to show up for, write an ad and **only pay when someone clicks**. But the highest bidder doesn’t always win: Google rewards quality too. Here are the three ingredients.

items.title: 1. The right searches
items.text: “Emergency electrician Dallas” is worth far more than “how does a circuit breaker work”. I target people ready to get in touch.

items.title: 2. An ad that persuades
items.text: A few characters to tell people why they should pick you: clear benefits, real proof and a call to action.

items.title: 3. A page that converts
items.text: Where people land after the click matters as much as the ad. A fast, clear page brings in more enquiries, and Google rewards it with a lower cost per click.

pricing.text: Lots of agencies charge a percentage of your ad spend: the more you spend, the more they make. Not me. **Management is a fixed fee**, so my only incentive is to make every cent of your budget work as hard as possible.

faq.title: Questions about Google Ads
faq.text: Can’t see yours? [Drop me a line](#contatti) and I’ll reply by the next business day.

items.question: How much budget do I need to start?
items.answer: It depends on your industry and area: in some markets a few euros a day is enough, in others you’ll need more to get useful data. The free review gives you a realistic estimate before you spend a thing.

items.question: How much does management cost?
items.answer: A fixed monthly fee, set in the quote based on the number and complexity of your campaigns. Never a percentage of your budget.

items.question: When will I see results?
items.answer: The first data arrives within days. Proper optimization usually takes a few weeks, the time it takes to gather enough clicks and conversions.

items.question: Do I own the Google Ads account?
items.answer: Yes. The account is in your name, you pay Google directly and I work on it with manager access. If you ever switch providers, everything stays with you.

items.question: Google Ads or SEO: which is better?
items.answer: They work best together: Google Ads gets results straight away but stops when you stop paying; SEO takes longer but lasts. The best strategy often combines both.

items.question: Can I pause the campaigns whenever I want?
items.answer: Yes, you can pause campaigns at any time, say when you’re closed or fully booked.
